blocking.claim: docs/22 line 116 (Step 4, Schedule paragraph): 'Demoting to a fixpoint before any re-promotion judges every loser in a round at its rank in the promoted table; the alternative, one demotion then re-promotion, lets a single created by a demotion be promoted over first, which lifts a later loser one slot and can change whether it pays.' The same sentence is in the resolve_rows docstring, candidate_selection.py lines 313-316 ('every loser in a round is judged at its evidence rank (its rank in the promoted table)'), and in the test comment at tests/test_candidate_selection.py lines 236-237.
blocking.evidence: The code does not judge later losers at their rank in the promoted table. resolve_rows (lines 328-336) calls _demote_once on the table as mutated by the earlier demotions of the same round, and _demote_once takes the loser's rank from its current index (line 281, _rank_points(j + 1)). A removal (lines 287-289, 291-293) or the drop of a lower duplicate single (lines 301-303) earlier in the walk shifts every row below it up, so a later loser is judged at a rank above its promoted-table rank, and the pays test can flip. This is the same class of lift the sentence attributes only to the step schedule. Measured on the probe's own universe and seed (policy_probe.random_pool, seed 20260926): in 57 of 3,000 pools a loser is judged at a rank other than its promoted-table rank; in 1 of 3,000 this changes the pays decision and the first ten rows of the file. On an 11-allele universe (five in one gene) it changes the file in 7 of 3,000 pools (seed 20260926) and 6 of 3,000 (seed 1). Worked pool (all synthetic; candidate = contig:position, tier, both lanes, native rank): 2:4000 B one 4; 1:4000 A one 2; 1:3000 A one 7; 2:3000 B one 4; 2:5000 B one 2; 1:2000 B both 7; 3:5000 A both 7; 4:7000 B both 4. Promoted table has 14 rows with the pair 2:3000+2:4000 at rank 11 and its winner 2:3000+2:5000 at rank 8. The first demotion call removes the pair 1:2000+1:3000 at rank 4 (both alleles claimed above). Every row below moves up one: the winner is now at rank 7 (partial 5) and the loser at rank 10 (full 10), 10 > 5, so the shipped code keeps it as a pair at rank 10 of the final file. Judged at its promoted-table rank 11, points(11) = 0 is not above 5 and the pair would be removed (both alleles claimed). The document's own stated rule (points(r) > 0.5 x points(q) with r the promoted-table rank) and the code disagree on this pool. The code is the pre-registered rule the module docstring says is checkable ('if the document and this module disagree, one of them is wrong'); the sentence in docs/22, the resolve_rows docstring and the test comment are what is wrong. The measured advantage of the batch schedule is unaffected (both schedules re-measured 0 below the plain sort, batch ahead on all eleven seeds).
blocking.repro: cd <worktree>; python3 - <<EOF with the pool above: from mva_prioritizer.candidate_selection import Candidate, order_rows, promote_rows, _demote_once; build the eight Candidates with recessive_annotation True; out, _ = promote_rows(order_rows(pool)); print the enumerated table; out, what = _demote_once(out) -> 'removed', 13 rows; out, what = _demote_once(out) -> None: the pair 2:3000+2:4000 stays at rank 10. Then apply the sentence by hand: at promoted rank 11 its points are 0, not above 0.5 x points(8) = 5, so the sentence says it is removed. Scratch driver used: <scratch>/review-c1c2c34/schedule_claim2.py and promrank.py (a copy of _demote_once that reads r from the promoted table instead of the current index; compare resolve_rows output on 3,000 random pools).
